items.stem: Which of the following statements about indentured servitude is true?
options: Indentured servitude was the means by which most Africans came to the New World.
Indentured servitude never attracted many people because its terms were too harsh.
Approximately half of all indentured servants died before earning their freedom.
Indenture was one of several systems used to distinguish house enslaved people from field enslaved people.
items.explanation: Indentured servitude promised freedom and a parcel of land to those who survived its seven-year term of service. However, fewer than half of indentured servants succeeded. Most worked in the fields performing grueling labor, and many died as a result. Indentured servitude was available only to English immigrants, and nearly 100,000 took advantage of it.

items.stem: The Mayflower Compact foreshadows the U.S. Constitution in which of the following ways?
options: It posits the source of government power in the people rather than in God.
It ensures both the right to free speech and the separation of church and state.
It limits the term of office for all government officials.
It establishes three branches of government in order to create a system of checks and balances.
items.explanation: The Mayflower Compact states that government derives its power from the consent of the governed, not from divine mandate. This distinguishes government under the Mayflower Compact from the monarchial government the Pilgrims left behind in England.

items.stem: The first important cash crop in the American colonies was
items.explanation: Virginia, one of the earliest colonies, developed around the tobacco trade; tobacco was the colonies’ first important cash crop. Choice (A), cotton, did not become a major export until the early 19th century, when the invention of the cotton gin made large-scale cotton farming practical.

items.stem: The philosophy of mercantilism holds that economic power resides primarily in
options: surplus labor power and control over raw materials
control of hard currency and a positive trade balance
the ability to extend and receive credit at favorable interest rates
domination of the slave trade and control of the shipping lanes
items.explanation: During the Colonial Era, the British subscribed to the economic theory of mercantilism, which held that a favorable balance of trade and control of hard currency were the keys to economic power. Ultimately, the theory of capitalism, famously championed by Adam Smith, supplanted mercantilism as the predominant economic theory of the West.

items.stem: Which of the following best facilitated British colonization of North America?
options: The defeat of the Spanish Armada
items.explanation: The defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 effectively ended Spain’s domination of the high seas and thus allowed England to establish colonies of its own. Spain’s military might had allowed it to predominate in the New World throughout the 16th century, thwarting England’s desire to achieve ascendancy. The Armada was the decisive victory by the English that shifted the balance of power in Europe and allowed them to become the preeminent 17th century imperial nation in North America.

items.stem: All of the following are examples of conflicts between colonists and Native American tribes EXCEPT
items.explanation: The Stono Uprising was an early slave rebellion (1739) in which enslaved Africans rose against their oppressors. The Stono Uprising is sometimes referred to as the Cato Rebellion.

items.stem: Which of the following colonies was NOT founded for reasons grounded in religious conflict?
items.explanation: Many of the northern colonies were founded in the 17th century by those seeking a haven from religious strife or persecution. In contrast, Georgia was founded in 1732 as a refuge for indebted prisoners and also as a buffer colony to protect the southern colonies from potential Spanish invasion.

items.stem: Colleges and universities during the colonial period were dedicated primarily to the training of
items.explanation: The purpose of America’s first colleges was to train homegrown clergy so that the colonies would no longer have to import their clergy from England. The four oldest extant colonial universities—Harvard, William & Mary, Yale, and Princeton—were all originally affiliated with specific Protestant faiths.

items.stem: Which of the following is the best explanation for why the British did not establish a powerful central government in the American colonies?
options: The British cared little how the colonists lived so long as the colonies remained a productive economic asset.
Britain feared that the colonists would rebel against any substantial government force that it established.
Few members of the British elite were willing to travel to the colonies, even for the opportunity to govern.
Britain gave the colonies a large measure of autonomy as a first step in transitioning the region to independence.
items.explanation: Provided the colonies continued to buy British goods and to supply the British with raw materials, England did not care how the colonies governed themselves. England did impose its will (through the vice-admiralty courts) when the colonies attempted to shirk their economic responsibilities but otherwise took a laissez-faire approach. As a result, the colonies developed a tradition of independence that contributed to their eventual rebellion against the Crown.

items.stem: Which of the following statements best defines the early interactions between English colonists and Native Americans in the New World?
options: English colonists viewed Native Americans as a potential workforce and largely aimed to enslave them in the regions they colonized.
English colonists largely avoided contact or relations with Native Americans as much as possible in the regions they colonized.
English colonists maintained friendly relations with Native Americans and sought alliances with them in the regions they colonized.
English colonists considered Native Americans as valuable trading partners and depended on their skills and knowledge with the land to their mutual benefit in the regions they colonized.
items.explanation: Unlike most other early European colonizing powers, English settlers aimed to avoid contact and relations with Native Americans. Choices (A), (C), and (D) describe the early interactions between Native Americans and the Spanish, French, and Dutch, respectively.

items.stem: The earliest European settlements in North America were largely centralized around New England, the Chesapeake Bay, and the St. Lawrence River except for those associated with which European power?
items.explanation: The Spanish extensively colonized the New World during the first two centuries following Columbus’s arrival in 1492. The first settlements for the French, English, and Dutch mostly centered around the region described.
